res227-122.summary: Louis XIII's proposals to the Duke of Savoy (Valtellina, help in case of rupture, Geneva), the French answer and the Duke's return from Avignon; Mirabel's talk with the Queen Mother on the deposit of the Valtellina forts, a Lorraine garrison and the capitulations of Aranjuez, the Catholic religion to be kept there; Richelieu, not of the King's Council, governs the Queen Mother.
res227-122.en:
Read in part: 82.2% of the cipher words by the project's count (sure words only, 13 Nov 2026: probable, restored and unresolved words are holes); 92.4% on the contributor's count of certain + probable (13 Nov 2026). {x} = probable word, [x] = restored word, […] = unresolved; italic = clear in the manuscript.

[…] of the proposals the King has made to the Duke of Savoy, which were: the settlement and restitution of the Valtellina;
the advantages that would follow from it for this King and his allies, {offering him} his assistance in case no settlement
were reached to his satisfaction. Likewise he {deals} with the Duke's quarrels, wishing that the {Most Christian} King settle
them, or else in case of a rupture favour his cause as he did in the past. He also {made} {great} instance to be given leave
and assistance for the enterprise of Geneva.

mss18428-13-15.summary: Early 1622, after Luynes's death: court gossip about Luynes's widow; Philip IV's order to send the French ladies home from Madrid and the Spanish servants from Paris; the Queen's confessor; Louis XIII's good faith and the capitulations of the Grisons treaties expected.
mss18428-13-15.en:
Same holes as reading.md: {x} = probable; [x] = restored; ‹…› = unresolved; italic = clear in the manuscript. Read in part (250 cipher words: 183 certain, 36 probable, 11 restored, 20 unresolved). A working translation, close to the Spanish; the key is not validated (see validation.txt).

Part A (images 13 right - 14 right).
The Marquis of Mirabel also ‹24›, for my men are not all angels, those ‹…› ‹…›, only those Your Lordship knows. Not only do I believe what Your Lordship writes me of Madame de ‹Jamuila›, since there are no Luyneses left in the world, {but} Your Lordship may also believe that as soon as this King {arrived}, the very same day, he {visited} her, and she made him many complaints, asking him how His Majesty could allow people to speak ill {of} her {husband} ‹…›, and she.
